answer: The copper test I would run is Signed darts league membership with match results: matches played across five seasons, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. What makes this stick is that matches played across five seasons cannot be faked in bulk — each proof is independent, and the inlet of independence is that one compromised proof endangers no other account. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the summit of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
